text:
sophia: quick sync — want alignment on the 'route governance launch canvas' for long-term platform routing. goal: agree gating and migration runway for multi-region + per-tenant isolation. high level proposals below, need decisions by EOD Friday.

kai: can you bullet the gates? i can validate SLO/infra impact quickly. :clock1:

sophia: sure. proposed gates (short):
- pilot: 3 customers on dedicated slices for 2 weeks
- resilience: cross-region failover test with <5% error budget burn in canary
- economics: per-tenant cost delta within threshold (<=15%)
- security/compliance: KMS + audit logs in private deploys

aleks: +1 on pilots. add a soft downgrade policy for noisy tenants so we don't evict immediately. also we should define "compatible variant" (quantized vs full) before launch.

jordan: important: define routing contract matrix. who owns runbooks when reroute happens? ops or customer success?

kai: initial SLOs to validate: p50/p95 latency per model family, request success rate, and cold-standby spin-up time. tentative numbers: p95 < 300ms for small models, <600ms for large; cold-standby spin < 90s. i'll run capacity calc once gates are final.

sophia: here's a minimal policy sketch to discuss (not prod-ready):
```yaml
policy_name: regional_governance_v0
priorities:
  - local
  - variant_compatible
  - regional_peers
  - cold_standby
max_total_latency_ms: 1200
tenant_controls:
  pin_to_region: optional
  burst_window_sec: 120
  quarantine_threshold: 0.2 # fraction of errors to trigger isolation
```

aleks: i like the quarantine_threshold idea but prefer absolute error counts + traffic-pattern checks to avoid noisy fraction for tiny tenants.

jordan: question on "variant_compatible": do we allow model downgrades (eg. 8-bit quant) that change output semantics? customers will push back. need explicit opt-in and a quality-monitoring rollback.

sophia: agreed. gating includes a quality regression check against canonical prompts. if regression > 3% we fail the gate.

kai: from infra: we also need a migration runway plan for tenants who request pinned regions. propose a 3-phase migration: sandbox -> shadow -> cutover with rollback window. timeline per-tenant ~48-72h plus validation.

aleks: customers asking for hard-pinning will pay for warm standby. add pricing note to migration playbook.

infra-bot: created ticket INFRA-5247 with checklist and links: https://go/redwood/infra/INFRA-5247. actions: add chaos tests, update canary job, add metrics dashboard.

sophia: decisions we need here:
1) final gate list (pilot/resilience/econ/security/quality)
2) definition of compatible variant and opt-in flow
3) migration runway template and cost model for warm standbys
4) ownership of runbooks for reroute events

kai: i can own SLO validation (1) and infra tests (3).

aleks: i'll draft the opt-in flow and quality rollback (2).

jordan: i'll own runbook ownership proposal (4) and coordinate with support.

sophia: perfect — i'll consolidate into a launch canvas doc and send to PMs + sales to collect pilot candidates. next sync Wednesday 10am.

aleks: small ask from Sales: can we include a per-tenant "burst credit" concept that temporarily increases capacity for a fee? may help landing enterprise pilots.

kai: feasible, but needs throttles and billing hooks. infra cost predictability will be rough; we should model scenarios.

sophia: noted. i'll add to the canvas as an optional commercial lever. thanks all. :sparkles:

jordan: ack, will start runbook draft and loop in support.

infra-bot: reminder: planned canary window opens Mon 03/30 00:00 UTC.

sophia: closing loop — i'll post the canvas doc link once updated. thanks everyone.
